statement: A no-silent-rescore guard keyed to a version string, whose golden fixture does not contain the shape that changed, in a different repository from the scanner that shipped, is a check that reports on something it did not examine. Three 0.4.9 fixes changed scoring under the calibrated default witan-rubric-v17 with no identifier bump; the cited guard lives in alfred, keys on WITAN_RUBRIC_VERSION, pins a fixture with `test: 'vitest run'` and test files, and runs against a diverged copy of the scanner — it could not fire. Measuring all 24 corpus rows found 3 moved under v17 in 0.4.9 and, checking the baseline against the published board, that 0.4.8 had already moved a headline (fastapi 3.1 to 3.0) with no entry either. Rule: a scoring guard must pin fixtures that exercise each behaviour a release changes, in the repository that ships, and a release that touches any file the scanner reads from must re-score the corpus before the version bump, not after a reader notices.

statement: A fix for a false positive that is measured only on the shape it was written for can ship a false negative in the opposite direction, and only a corpus-wide delta shows it. The test-script content check was written so npm's placeholder (`echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`) stops scoring as a test capability; its guard tests used the placeholder and `vitest run`. Re-scoring the 24-row corpus found the placeholder on zero rows and three rows losing B3.ci_script_depth for real, delegating test scripts (`grunt test --verbose`, `pnpm test-unit && …`, a monorepo task runner) that the runner allowlist does not name. The fix converted 'credits a placeholder' into 'does not credit delegation' — a new false assertion of absence, in the direction that lowers a score. Rule: a detector change earns its guard against the shapes it will meet on the corpus, not only the shape that motivated it; run the corpus before declaring the fix bounded.

statement: A reproduction check that compares whole report objects fires on every row the moment any field is added between the two producers, and a check that fires regardless of input examined nothing. The 0.4.9 delta harness's baseline-vs-published-board check compared entire reports; 0.4.8 had added a `derivation` field to every finding, so it said DIFFERS on 24 of 24 rows while the real four discrepancies were found by hand and the automation was quoted as if it had found them. The reviewer caught it, not the author. The same harness imported its scanner by a path that resolved only once copied to a worktree root, so 'run via pnpm exec tsx' was true of the run and false of the committed file. Rule: compare at the level the claim is made (headline, per-criterion score/status, per-metric value), state the expected pass count before running, verify the check reproduces what a hand inspection found (20 of 24, four named), and print the resolved scanner path and git HEAD before the first number.
